display.title: Episode 487: The Stone for the Beis HaMikdash (The Three Weeks)
display.summary_short: Poor Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa finds a perfect stone for the Beis HaMikdash, and angels carry it to Yerushalayim once he adds his little finger: try your best and Hashem will do the rest.
display.summary_long: Broadcast in the middle of the Three Weeks, without music. Uncle Yossi explains that the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed for lack of Ahavas Yisroel, and that loving one another will bring the Geulah. The story, told in two parts around the Shema and tzedakah, is about Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa, who is too poor to bring a gift for the building of the Beis HaMikdash. He finds a perfectly squared stone that could be a cornerstone, but it is far too heavy. Five strangers, really angels, offer to carry it, but it will not move until he places his own little finger under it; then it floats all the way to Yerushalayim. Every mitzvah adds a stone to the third Beis HaMikdash, and 'you try your best and Hashem will do the rest.' A boy from Tzivos Hashem says the Shema between the parts. Uncle Yossi then explains Rosh Chodesh Av, the Alter Rebbe's teaching that Hashem, like a parent, delights most when His children love each other, and the Rambam's principle of awaiting Moshiach, when Tisha B'Av will become a Yom Tov. The show ends with an invitation to the Tzivos Hashem summer rally and candle-lighting time.
display.lesson: Do your part, even a little, and Hashem will do the rest; every mitzvah adds a stone to the third Beis HaMikdash.

date.note: 'This coming Friday is Rosh Chodesh Av' (1 Av 5751 = Friday 12 July 1991); rally announced for 'Sunday, July 28th', which fits 1991. A Tuesday.

advisories.note: Talks about the Three Weeks and the destruction of the Beis HaMikdash.

sources_cited.note: The story of Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa's stone, told as 'a true story as told by our Chachamim'.
The Beis HaMikdash was destroyed because of baseless hatred.
'You are children to Hashem your G-d.'
The Alter Rebbe: Hashem, like a parent, takes the greatest pleasure in His children loving one another.
The Rambam's principle of faith in the coming of Moshiach.
